seo.title: What is a design system?
seo.description: A design system is the agreed set of colours, type, spacing and components that every page of a product is built from.

definition: A design system is the agreed set of colours, type, spacing and components that every page of a product is built from.
answerBlock: A design system is the agreed set of colours, type, spacing and components that every page of a product is built from. It is not a style guide in a slide deck. It is code and tokens that designers and developers both use, so a button behaves the same way wherever it appears.

body.heading: What does a design system contain?
paragraphs: Tokens first: the colour values, type faces, sizes, spacing steps and radii, each with a name. Then components built from those tokens: buttons, form fields, cards, tables, dialogs, each with its states and its accessibility behaviour already decided.

Around them sit the rules. Which colour is reserved for outcome figures and never used for decoration. Which heading level a card title takes. How motion behaves for someone who has asked their device to reduce it. The rules are what keep the system from drifting back into one-off pages.
A design system is a live dependency, not a document. When a token changes, every page that uses it changes, which is the point.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: The saving is in the second, tenth and fiftieth page. Once the components exist, a new template is assembled rather than designed from nothing, and quality does not depend on who happened to build it.
It also keeps a brand intact across a marketing site, an application and documentation, which is exactly where brands normally fall apart.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: Truvia Labs rebuilt its marketing site, documentation and in-app onboarding on one design system, so releases stopped breaking the brand and organic sessions grew 3.1 times.

service.title: Custom website development
service.line: Research-led design built around how your buyers actually decide, not around a template's section order.

terms.definition: Accessibility means a website can be used by people with disabilities, and WCAG is the published standard that defines what that requires.
Information architecture is how a site is organised: what pages exist, how they are grouped, and what each one is called.
Responsive design means one website that rearranges itself to work on any screen, from a phone to a wide monitor.
A wireframe is a deliberately plain layout of a page that settles what is on it and in what order, before anyone decides how it looks.
